evidence:
Row 35's defining-behavior and independent-server-readback coverage is strong, but required process durability is not reliably proven. Paths below use T=.qc-cache/hireops-2026-10-01-transaction-hardening-r2/task and R=qc/runs/hireops-2026-10-01-transaction-hardening-r2. Public instruction.md:3,9,11 and environment/instructions/hireops_rules.md:384,439,467-478 require saved previews, records and original receipts across restart. T/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:938 grades the fully funded coordinated exchange; :1019 requires an independent signed-in preview read; :1109-1127 require fresh-context receipt/member history readback; :929 and :1154 grade restart durability and original-result replay. T/tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:9,15 explicitly use independent empty contexts, and :49 requires one real restart. T/tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:23-25 rejects no-op/browser-only state. Routes, generated identities and optional operational seed imports are not fixed, so a valid app with different routes/IDs or initially empty operations is not excluded by these protocols.

The failure is in the restart witness used by those criteria: T/tests/test.sh:153-159 sends TERM and waits about five seconds but neither kills nor rejects a still-running old process; :160-183 launches another process and accepts any HTTP responder without checking that the replacement is alive. T/tests/tools/restart_mcp.py:45-47 converts helper exit zero into a claim of successful relaunch. The wrapper is byte-identical to the frozen template (SHA256 bd68259276ca4b034654efc8a1723a4e702ed62dbe590af6201565f43eabe5aa), so this is an inherited harness blocker, not permission to alter shared policy.

Verified current raw-evidence-index hashes: R/per-row-review/evidence/21/controlled-recheck/restart-retains-old-process/restart-observation.json SHA256 063c493fad28e987ac4e6b1c2bb6f0c9bc5ace97dfd87559cb644e97c3d61ab2 records helper returncode=0 with before PID=189 and after PID=189; its logs/app-restart.log SHA256 d1ac2ff49ef694c86b597a44689218477aec9bf2eb3f728437a9b0d043d1eb51 records replacement EADDRINUSE followed by ready=1. The driver (probe-v2.py SHA256 5b674556e7ad9efbffe16675cc738c93f61ac281d96dbb23cfa5008b9af31714, lines 25-39) runs the generated helper and separately reads the answering process, using a fixture that ignores TERM. Its run-manifest SHA256 7b5a55799d8ef646888692005f12083e49e5c26478452c063ec4256756a185c1 binds the frozen test.sh hash. The normal control changed PID24 to52 (restart-normal/restart-observation.json SHA256 5247688c9e8e2d618e599f80789c90c88d72b7a035e405f8ab2e1f1d33cb7ffa). These are raw harness observations with stubbed RewardKit, not actual app scores.

Positive product evidence is preserved: R/local/batch-domain.cjs:117-119 stops/restarts the golden and compares complete financial records, saved drafts and the original receipt; results.json SHA256 a44c0bf81b27981d9bf1d63239f8b7ce7da5733d6d70aef425e2350a76b7732f reports success. R/local/batch-ui/results.json SHA256 c80c06dc937a3e32d8f46af020e75f3cc36d37a2a44e5eeebbf1ba058857aae5 reports UI prepare/commit, same-operation lost-response retry and independent Auditor readback; its driver was inspected. All 14 recorded solution file hashes match the frozen files. R/local/install-lifecycle/results.json SHA256 52b5ba96bded2e133fe4ec16117c150d46673f70ce31284169193f478c73e9f9 records actual MCP golden PID21->97 with saved data retained. The golden evidence establishes working examples, but cannot refute the verified old-process false positive. No full configured judge/Oracle/model score is claimed.
counterexample: A working HireOps implementation could keep all operational records and immutable receipts only in server memory while trapping SIGTERM. Independent-browser sign-ins and the real transaction criteria would succeed. At P10 the helper can return success while the same old process answers every read and original-receipt retry, so hro_restart and hro_change_retry_restart can credit persistence even though all data would disappear on a real process replacement. The indexed PID189->189/EADDRINUSE observation confirms the enabling mechanism, not a configured grade of that complete weak app. Conforming alternative assessed: a SQLite-backed app may take longer than five seconds to finish graceful shutdown; no public rule sets that shutdown deadline. The corresponding indexed slow-shutdown fixture (SHA256 e5d7700af4e53d5c280f7edbb0ebb24c0eace1def6044064e795189878af0328) also returns success while still on PID82, so later disappearance or failed readback could reflect harness lifecycle handling rather than lost durable data. Different routes, generated IDs and optional empty operational seed remain accepted by the task-specific durability procedures.
suggested_fix: Have the shared harness owner supply an approved restart helper that verifies old process termination, performs bounded escalation when needed, confirms the replacement remains alive and owns readiness, then rebind the candidate and rerun both normal-durable and resistant-memory/slow-shutdown witnesses; preserve template-controlled files and scoring policy until that shared correction is authorized.
